questions.q: What is Denmark's national direct debit scheme called?
questions.reason: Betalingsservice, run by Nets, is Denmark's direct debit. Autogiro is Swedish and AvtaleGiro is Norwegian.

questions.q: What is Sweden's direct debit scheme called?
questions.reason: Autogiro runs through Bankgirot in Sweden.

questions.q: What is Norway's direct debit scheme called?
questions.reason: AvtaleGiro is Norway's direct debit, often combined with eFaktura.

questions.q: Which mobile payment app is Swedish?
questions.reason: Swish is owned by the big Swedish banks. Vipps is Norwegian; MobilePay is Danish.

questions.q: Which mobile payment app is Norwegian?
questions.reason: Vipps is Norwegian. It merged with MobilePay into the company Vipps MobilePay.

questions.q: What is the Norwegian payment reference number called?
questions.reason: KID (customer identification) tells the insurer whose payment it is.

questions.q: What is the Swedish payment reference number on a Bankgiro bill called?
questions.reason: Customers pay to the insurer's Bankgiro number with an OCR number.

questions.q: What is a Danish payment slip with a reference number called?
questions.reason: The +71 type carries a payment ID that FSCD uses to match the payment.

questions.q: Why do reference numbers end with a check digit?
options: So a mistyped number can be rejected before the money is sent
questions.reason: The check digit catches typing mistakes early, which prevents unmatched payments.

questions.q: In direct debit, who starts the payment?
options: The insurer, through FSCD's payment run
questions.reason: After a one-time mandate, FSCD's payment run sends the collection file every time.

questions.q: What is a mandate in direct debit?
options: The customer's one-time permission to collect
questions.reason: Called tilmelding (DK), medgivande (SE) or avtale (NO).

questions.q: Ingrid's AvtaleGiro maximum is NOK 2,000. The insurer tries to collect NOK 2,500. What happens?
questions.reason: AvtaleGiro lets the customer set a maximum per payment. A BA must check it when premiums go up.

questions.q: Which file does Bankgirot send with incoming Swedish payments?
questions.reason: FSCD loads the BgMax file as a payment lot and matches each payment by its OCR number.

questions.q: A payment arrives with no usable reference. Where does it go in FSCD?
options: The clarification queue for manual work
It is sent back to the customer at once
questions.reason: Missing references are the biggest everyday pain in collections.

questions.q: Which currencies do Denmark, Sweden and Norway use?
questions.reason: None of the three uses the euro.

questions.q: What is the usual way insurers pay claims in the Nordics?
options: Bank transfer (plus Swish payouts in Sweden)
questions.reason: Payouts are almost always bank transfers. In Sweden Swish payout is also popular.

questions.q: Which international file format is often used for outgoing payments?
questions.reason: In SAP these files are created by the Payment Medium Workbench.

questions.q: Which SAP tool creates the bank payment files?
questions.reason: One FSCD payment run can produce files for all three countries through the Payment Medium Workbench.

questions.q: Which Swedish digital mailbox often receives bills?
questions.reason: Kivra is Swedish, e-Boks is Danish and Digipost is Norwegian.

questions.q: Which digital mailbox is Danish?
questions.reason: In the main guide, Mette's level 2 reminder letter goes to e-Boks.

questions.q: How does FSCD learn that a MobilePay, Swish or Vipps payment arrived?
options: Through a settlement report or bank statement file
questions.reason: The money moves fast, but FSCD still learns through a file, so the policy number in the payment is key.

questions.q: Which FSCD transaction loads failed direct debits as a batch?
questions.reason: FP05 loads incoming payments as payment lots; FP09 loads returns.

questions.q: Erik's stolen bike claim of SEK 3,500 is paid in seconds. Which method?
questions.reason: Swedish insurers can pay claims straight to a mobile number with Swish payout.

questions.q: A claim payout fails because of a wrong account number. What happens in FSCD?
options: The payable re-opens so it can be corrected and paid again
questions.reason: The bank rejects it, the payable re-opens, someone fixes the bank details and the next run pays again.

questions.q: Which of these is a Norwegian debit card scheme?
questions.reason: BankAxept is Norwegian; Dankort is Danish.

questions.q: In the four families of payment methods, eFaktura belongs to...
questions.reason: An e-invoice puts the bill straight into the customer's netbank, ready to approve.
